tone_patterns: Formal, standards-led tone that anchors the section in IFRS requirements before describing the organisation’s approach
Balanced assurance-oriented language emphasizing clarity, completeness, transparency, and accountability
Forward-looking but cautious phrasing when discussing planned enhancements (e.g., indicating intent and ongoing work rather than guarantees)
Stakeholder-usefulness framing: explains how disclosures help users assess resilience, governance, and decision-usefulness
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a short contextual overview explaining why the disclosures are required and what they enable users to evaluate
Separates IFRS S1 (broad sustainability metrics) from IFRS S2 (climate-specific metrics) in adjacent sentences/paragraphs to clarify scope
Includes an ‘approach’ paragraph describing how metrics are selected (relevance/materiality lens) and how targets are set (ambitious yet achievable framing)
Adds a short subsection noting alignment with other frameworks (e.g., GRI/SASB) as a bridge between legacy reporting and IFRS-aligned reporting
Includes a methodology/transparency paragraph referencing data collection methods and noting changes to standards/metrics where relevant
Ends the narrative lead-in with a data ‘as of’ timestamp and an update cadence/location statement before presenting tables
heading_patterns: Section opener uses a large numeric chapter marker paired with a two-line title (chapter number + section name)
Repeats the section title at the top of the next page as a running header for continuity
Uses decimal subsection numbering (e.g., 5.1, 5.2) with short, functional titles (e.g., Overview; Sustainability-related metrics and targets)
Subsection headings are concise and act as signposts rather than descriptive sentences
table_patterns: Primary disclosure delivered via multi-page tabular register of metrics rather than narrative
Consistent column set across pages: Metric | Metric Definition | Reporting-period Value | Source framework/type | Internal source document | Mapping to report section
Metric names are short labels; definitions provide clarifying detail and scope boundaries
Values column supports mixed data types (percentages, counts, currency/targets, and qualitative statements) within the same table structure
Source column distinguishes between external frameworks (e.g., standards) and internal metrics; internal source document column points to where supporting detail resides
Includes a ‘mapping to report section’ column that categorizes each metric to a disclosure pillar/theme (e.g., governance/risk/strategy) to aid navigation
Allows multi-line cells and bullet lists inside cells for policy/process descriptions when a metric is qualitative
Uses repeated table header rows on subsequent pages to maintain readability across page breaks
Table continues across pages with consistent styling and alignment; page footer repeats section title and page number
figure_or_diagram_patterns: No charts/diagrams used in the excerpt; emphasis is on tabular disclosure rather than visual analytics
If visuals are absent, the section relies on structured tables and clear headings to provide navigability
pdf_layout_patterns: Chapter divider page includes prominent chapter number and stacked title, functioning as a visual break between major sections
Running header repeats the section title on content pages for orientation
Page footer includes section title, page number, and report identifier line; consistent across pages
Tables span full page width with clear column boundaries; long text wraps within cells rather than overflowing
Multi-page tables maintain consistent column widths and repeat headers to support scanning
Whitespace and line breaks are used to separate narrative lead-in from the table block
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses standards-referencing language to justify disclosure scope (e.g., ‘required to disclose’ framing) without over-claiming performance
Explains the purpose of disclosures in user-centric terms (assessment of resilience, governance, risk management, strategic alignment)
States that metrics are selected systematically based on relevance to operations and impacts (materiality-style rationale)
Pairs metrics with targets and describes targets as measurable and time-bound where applicable, while keeping wording cautious
Includes transparency statements about methodologies and changes in metrics/standards over time
Provides a clear ‘data current as of’ statement and indicates planned update timing/channel
evidence_presentation_patterns: Evidence is presented through traceability: each metric links to (1) an external framework/source type and (2) an internal document/source location
Cross-referencing approach: ‘mapping to report section’ acts as an internal index to where narrative context is provided
Where quantitative data is not applicable, the table permits a qualitative disclosure statement in the value/notes area
Uses structured definitions to reduce ambiguity and support comparability across periods
section_specific_observations: The section functions as a disclosure index/register: a consolidated list of metrics with definitions, values, and traceability metadata
Narrative content is brief and primarily sets context, scope, and data governance expectations before the tables
The design prioritizes auditability and navigation over storytelling (framework source + internal source + mapping fields)
things_to_avoid_copying: Any organisation name, report title line, or branded footer text
Any specific metric values, targets, dates, currencies, or time horizons
Any specific policy descriptions, hotline/contact details, email addresses, or named roles
Any claims about compliance, performance, ambition level, or stakeholder outcomes that are specific to the reference entity
Any exact metric list, metric wording, or framework mapping choices that reflect the reference entity’s material topics
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Entity name and report identifier appearing in footers
Specific reporting ‘as of’ date and future update timing
Specific metric values (percentages, counts, currency targets) and any time-bound targets
Specific internal document names used as sources
Specific governance composition details and any demographic breakdowns
Specific policy channel details (phone numbers, email addresses, named functions)
Specific framework references used in combination with particular metrics (kept only as generic ‘external frameworks’ pattern)
